solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Work in theatre alongside father and sons

parts.note: by means beside, as in sitting by the fire
pa is an informal word for a dad
S is the standard abbreviation for son; two sons give two of them

explanation.surface: A family business: someone working in a theatre with dad and the boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' here is the operating theatre, not the stage: the definition is a piece of surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart bypass is a common surgical operation, the kind of work done in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Language graduate not missing old university

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate's degree

indicators.note: missing says the letter for old drops out of the word not

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion

explanation.surface: A graduate who never misses their old university, described in terms of the language they speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes O out of NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantu is a large family of African tongues, including Swahili and Zulu.

clue.text: Curtailed piggy one's mushrooms

indicators.note: curtailed means the tail, the final letter, is cut off the word for piggy

parts.note: porcine means pig-like
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A greedy little pig has had its share of the mushrooms cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtailed' drops the final E of PORCINE, giving PORCIN; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcini are prized Italian ceps, the plural being the usual name for these edible fungi.

clue.text: Dog training runs, each involving an unspecified number

indicators.note: involving means the shuffled letters wrap around the unknown quantity
training reshapes something, so the letters of runs and each are rearranged

parts.note: in algebra z, like x and y, stands for an unknown number

explanation.surface: A dog-training class doing runs, each with some number of repetitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' looks like the dog class but is the anagram signal; algebra's z stands for any number.
explanation.definitionFit: The schnauzer is a German breed of terrier-like hound with a bearded muzzle.

clue.text: Dated model, holding back a state of excitement

indicators.note: held back here means the two words are written in the opposite direction

parts.note: if you dated someone you saw them, went out with them
to model for an artist is to sit

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned model holds back, caught in a state of nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses SAWSIT. 'Dated' looks like old-fashioned but means went out with.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiswas is British slang for a flustered, confused state, a tizzy; it was also a 1970s children's TV show.

clue.text: Alphabetical registry actually excluding editor on Times

indicators.note: excluding says the editor's abbreviation is left out of the word

parts.note: indeed means in fact, actually
x is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A newspaper's list being kept by The Times without its editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluding' removes ED from INDEED, leaving IND. 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An index is an alphabetical list of a book's topics with page references.

clue.text: Inform the Catalan about supporting card game

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means placed below the other piece

parts.note: whist is a trick-taking card game

indicators.note: about turns the Catalan article round

parts.note: el is the Catalan for the

explanation.surface: Someone tells the Catalan a few things while backing a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the article round; in a down clue 'supporting' means placed beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow the whistle is to inform on wrongdoing, and the single word can carry that sense.

clue.text: US writer's drinking vessel supplied with running water

parts.note: a stein is a large beer mug
beck is a northern English word for a stream

explanation.surface: An American author's beer mug, provided with a tap of running water.
explanation.walkthrough: BECK is a northern English and Scots word for a brook. The 's is 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck was the American novelist of The Grapes of Wrath.

clue.text: Some disturbed by roguish lawlessness

indicators.note: disturbed by means broken into by the next word's synonym

parts.note: any as in have you got any, some
arch means mischievous, roguish

explanation.surface: Some people are disturbed by a roguish breakdown of law and order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed by' means broken into: the roguish word splits the other after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is the absence of government and order: lawlessness is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Notice bog close to extractor fan

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
a mire is a bog or swamp

indicators.note: close to picks the final letter of extractor

explanation.surface: Instructions to spot that a bathroom sits right next to the extractor fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bog' is British slang for a toilet, which fits the extractor fan; here it is a swamp. 'fan' is the definition, not part of the appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan of someone is their devoted follower, someone who looks up to them.

clue.text: Ex-pupil on bass got Ali to change musical accompaniment

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

indicators.note: to change tells us the letters of got Ali are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former pupil, playing bass, got Ali to switch the musical backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges GOT ALI into LIGATO.
explanation.definitionFit: An obbligato is an essential instrumental part accompanying a melody, often a solo line.

clue.text: Perhaps Oliver or Annie scrap noisy old toy

parts.note: Oliver! and Annie are both stage musicals, examples shown by perhaps
to scrap is to fight, to box

explanation.surface: Throw out the clattering old toy from a stage show like Oliver or Annie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like throw away but means fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical box is a traditional toy that plays a tune on a comb when wound up.

clue.text: Fish and quinoa regularly served on time

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of quinoa

explanation.surface: A meal of fish with quinoa, dished up punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of QUINOA, UNA, which sit after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large sea fish of the mackerel family, eaten fresh or canned.

clue.text: Surge of intense activity brightened boring business, one conceded

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the synonym goes inside
conceded means given up, so the letter for one is dropped

parts.note: biz is informal shorthand for business
I is the Roman numeral one
lit means lit up, brightened

explanation.surface: A rush of work cheered up a dull firm, though one point was given away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceded' drops the one; 'boring' looks like dull but means piercing.
explanation.definitionFit: A blitz is a sudden concentrated effort, from the German word for lightning in wartime.

clue.text: Composer extremely bothersome, repositioning the heater

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme, outer letters of bothersome
repositioning moves the letters of the around

parts.note: an oven is a heater for cooking

explanation.surface: A very annoying problem: moving the heater around the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives BE from bothersome; 'repositioning' turns THE into ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludwig van Beethoven was the German composer of nine symphonies.

clue.text: Person in audience to record Frenchman backing

parts.note: to list is to record in writing

indicators.note: backing means the name is written back to front

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A member of the audience records a Frenchman supporting the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses RENE to ENER. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in an audience hears what is said or played, so is one who hears attentively.

clue.text: Dicky needs to dress one of five kids in sparkly clothing?

indicators.note: to dress means to put clothes round, so the jumble wraps the child
dicky is British slang for shaky or faulty, so the letters of needs are rearranged

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five children born together

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky must dress one of a set of quintuplets in glittery clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but is British slang for unsound, the anagram signal; 'to dress' means to wrap round.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes covered with sequins, small shiny discs, are sparkly; the question mark flags the loose phrasing.

clue.text: Casual golfer welcomes annual round — jumpers are needed for this

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the jumble holds the abbreviation
casual here means loosely arranged, so the letters of golfer are rearranged
round means turned about, so the two letters for yearly are reversed

parts.note: pa, per annum, means yearly

explanation.surface: A relaxed golfer takes on a yearly round where sweaters are required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casual' is the anagram signal, 'round' the reversal and 'welcomes' the insertion. 'jumpers' suggests woollies; they are people leaping over backs.
explanation.definitionFit: In the playground game, children vault over each other's bent backs, so jumpers are essential.

clue.text: One moves laboriously outside in Pontypool, wanting more rum

indicators.note: outside in picks the outside letters of the Welsh town's name

parts.note: rum means strange, so more rum means odder

explanation.surface: A slow walker in a Welsh town wants more rum.
explanation.walkthrough: PONTYPOOL is a town in south Wales. 'rum' looks like the drink but means odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A plodder walks heavily and slowly, or works steadily and without flair.

clue.text: Cry coming from Donald, possibly a charlatan

definitions.meaning: Donald Duck's call is the noise a duck makes
a fraud passing as a doctor

explanation.surface: Donald shouts out, possibly at a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A duck's call is its typical noise, and a fake doctor is a long-standing slang term for an impostor.

clue.text: Worry intensely since returning in London area

parts.note: ago as in long since, long ago

indicators.note: returning means the little word in is written backwards

parts.note: SE is the south-east London postal district

explanation.surface: Worrying hard ever since moving back to a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses IN to NI. SE is London's south-east postal area.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to suffer great mental anguish over a decision, to fret deeply.

clue.text: Wrap up eggs and drive away

parts.note: wrap up is slang for be quiet, the same as sh
O looks like an egg, so two eggs are two Os

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction: wrap up some eggs and take them off in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap up' is British slang for shut up, as well as cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is the word or action used to chase off an animal or person, to send it away.

clue.text: Abandoned plane, reassembled on-site, departs

parts.note: a jet is an aeroplane

indicators.note: reassembled says the letters of on-site are put together in a new order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables

explanation.surface: An aircraft left behind, rebuilt where it stood, takes off again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reassembled' rearranges ONSITE into TISONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw away or discard, so something jettisoned has been cast aside.

clue.text: Project written by American about new military government

indicators.note: about means going round the abbreviation for new

parts.note: to jut is to project, stick out

explanation.surface: A plan drafted by an American concerning a new army regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside JUT; 'written by' sets A under it. 'Project' looks like a scheme but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A junta is a group of officers ruling a country after seizing power.

clue.text: Raise stern of frigate reportedly destroyed

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a ship, so this takes the last letter of frigate
reportedly means the word that follows is heard, not seen

parts.note: wrecked means destroyed

explanation.surface: Lifting the back of a warship that was said to have been sunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives RECT, said like WRECKED. 'stern' fits the ship but just means last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect something is to build it or set it upright, to raise it.

clue.text: Short recording in medical department that can be seen

indicators.note: in means placed inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: short says the word for a recording loses its ending

parts.note: a video is a recording

explanation.surface: A brief clip in a hospital department, available for viewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' takes off only the final letter, and 'in' puts what remains inside the ear, nose and throat department.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plain, obvious, visible to anyone who looks.

clue.text: Diane moved into centre of Bude by herself

indicators.note: into means the jumble goes inside the middle letters
centre of picks the middle letters of the Cornish town's name
moved says the letters of Diane are shifted around

explanation.surface: Diane moved to the middle of Bude all on her own.
explanation.walkthrough: BUDE is a seaside town in Cornwall; its centre is UD. 'moved' rearranges DIANE into NAIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unaided means doing it alone, without any help, as by herself.

clue.text: Golden castle maybe following new architectural style

indicators.note: following means coming after, here after the letter for new

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a castle, the rook, is one example of a chess man

explanation.surface: A golden castle built in the wake of a new style of building.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry; a chess castle is a MAN, a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman architecture is the Romanesque style, with round arches, brought to England after 1066.

clue.text: Present opening is after this period

indicators.note: is after places the word for opening after the era's label

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the present era
a vent is an opening for air

explanation.surface: Christmas presents get opened only once this season is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift but is AD, our present era.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is the season of four weeks leading up to Christmas in the Christian calendar.
